functions.name: core_recovery_note_boot
functions.brief: Account for this boot and return the running strike count. Call once, very early in core_init(), before clocks/user code.

functions.name: core_recovery_over_limit
functions.brief: True once we've had enough consecutive watchdog resets to give up on the app.

functions.name: core_recovery_clear
functions.brief: Clear the strike counter now. core_watchdog_feed() already does this once the app has run healthy for max(10 s, 2x the timeout); call this only to declare health earlier than that.

functions.name: hal_dfu_jump_to_rom
functions.brief: Jump to the STM32 ROM (system memory) bootloader. Does not return. Called from core_init() when ROM_DFU is enabled and the DFU magic was found. Runs before ANY peripheral or clock init, so the MCU is in near-reset state. The ROM bootloader configures its own clocks (HSI48 + CRS for USB) and enumerates as 0483:DF11 with DfuSe. L4 (Cortex-M4): Remaps system memory to 0x00000000 via SYSCFG_MEMRMP, then jumps. The remap ensures the ROM bootloader reads its own vectors from address 0 and doesn't bounce back to flash. H5 (Cortex-M33): No MEMRMP equivalent in SBS. Instead, sets VTOR directly to the ROM bootloader base — the M33 always respects VTOR for vector fetches, so no memory remap is needed. Only reached with BOOT0 low: with BOOT0 high the touch's reset already lands in the ROM (RM0481 §4.1, Table 23).

functions.name: hal_dfu_reboot
functions.brief: Reboot into DFU mode. Does not return. Writes the DFU magic to a reserved SRAM address, then triggers a system reset. SRAM survives system reset, so the bootloader (custom or ROM) will see the magic on the next boot.

functions.name: hal_recovery_strikes
functions.brief: Consecutive watchdog-reset strikes carried across warm reset (0 if cold).

functions.name: hal_recovery_valid
functions.brief: True if the recovery words survived a warm reset (tag valid).

functions.name: hal_recovery_set_strikes
functions.brief: Set the strike count and stamp the validity tag.

functions.name: hal_recovery_stash_cause
functions.brief: Stash whether this boot was a watchdog reset (so the app's core_watchdog_caused_reset() still works after we clear the HW flag).

functions.name: hal_recovery_stashed_cause
functions.brief: Read back the stashed reset cause (1 = watchdog).
